p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines what a *comparative research document* is, why the genre exists, the five laws every such document obeys, when to write one, and how the study connects to the roadmap without ever ratifying itself.

p.A-RESEARCH-DOCUMENT-IS-A-SELF-CONTAINED-: A comparative research document is a **self-contained, evergreen study of one external system** — a competitor, a predecessor, an adjacent tool that occupies ground near yours.

p.IT-INVENTORIES-QUOTES-MEASURES-AND-TRANS: It inventories what that system does, quotes it in its own words, measures it in two directions against your own project, and translates the actionable findings into numbered roadmap proposals.

p.THE-DOCUMENT-IS-WRITTEN-TO-OUTLAST-ITS-S: The document is written to be **re-readable months after publication without referring to the original sources, and to outlast any one external project's URL stability**.

item.ROT-PRODUCTS-GET-ACQUIRED-AND-DELETED: whole products get acquired and deleted.

p.a-study-that-links-out-expires: A study that merely links out is a study that expires.

p.a-quoted-study-stands-after-the-links-ro: A study that quotes verbatim with dates is a study that stands on its own after the links rot.

p.three-costs-justify-the-effort-lead: Three costs justify the effort of a full study over a quick glance:

item.COST-UNEXAMINED-COMPETITORS-COST-ROADMAP: **Unexamined competitors cost roadmap mistakes.** Building in a space someone else already occupies, without knowing what they built, means re-discovering their dead ends at your own expense — or missing the one feature that was the whole point.

item.COST-EXAMINED-COMPETITORS-YIELD-DELTAS: **Examined competitors yield deltas.** Understanding what a rival does well — *and what it does not* — is load-bearing intelligence for your own roadmap. Every gap you find is a candidate decision: close it, decline it on record, or note it as already led.

item.COST-THE-STUDY-MUST-OUTLIVE-LINK-ROT: **The study must outlive link rot and staff turnover.** The person who did the research leaves; the URL 404s; the competitor pivots. What remains is the document, and the document is only worth keeping if it is complete on its own terms.

p.EVERY-DOCUMENT-OBEYS-ALL-FIVE-LAWS: Every comparative research document obeys all five.

p.the-laws-separate-a-study-from-a-rant: They are what separate a study from a bookmark dump or a competitive-envy rant.

p.LAW-ONE-THE-DOCUMENT-MUST-STAND-WHEN-ITS: The document must stand when its sources vanish.

p.LAW-ONE-QUOTE-VERBATIM-WITH-AN-ACCESS-DA: Quote the subject **verbatim in fenced blocks, each carrying an access date**, rather than linking and trusting the link.

p.LAW-ONE-A-FUTURE-READER-RECONSTRUCTS-WIT: A future reader with no network access, opening the file a year later, must be able to reconstruct what the subject claimed without fetching anything.

p.LAW-ONE-LINKS-ARE-POINTERS-QUOTES-ARE-EV: Links are pointers for refresh; quotes are the evidence of record.

p.LAW-TWO-THE-SUBJECT-SPEAKS-BEFORE-IT-IS-: The subject speaks **in its own words before it is judged**.

p.LAW-TWO-PRESENT-THE-QUOTE-THEN-ANALYZE: Present the verbatim quote — the pitch, the feature description, the design claim — and only *then* analyze, praise, or fault it.

p.critiquing-a-paraphrase-is-critiquing-a-: Critiquing a paraphrase is critiquing a straw man: the paraphrase is already your reading, and a reader cannot check your judgement against a summary you wrote.

p.LAW-TWO-QUOTE-THEN-JUDGE-EVERY-TIME: Quote, then judge, in that order, every time.

item.LAW-THREE-A-SECTION-FOR-WHERE-YOU-TRAIL: a section for where you trail the subject,

item.LAW-THREE-A-SECTION-FOR-WHERE-YOU-LEAD: and a section for where you lead it.

p.one-directional-gap-analysis-is-advocacy: One-directional gap analysis is not analysis — it is advocacy:

p.WHERE-YOU-LEAD-DESERVES-THE-SAME-RIGOR: Where you lead deserves the same rigor as where you trail: name the decision you made that they did not, and say why it matters.

p.envy-blinds-you-to-the-moat-you-already-: Envy in one direction blinds you to the moat you already have.

p.LAW-FOUR-FINDINGS-BECOME-NUMBERED-PRIORI: Actionable findings become **numbered roadmap deltas**, each with a **priority** and a **target home** — "maps to a future spec section", not a change ratified here.

p.LAW-FOUR-THE-DOCUMENT-PROPOSES-IT-DOES-N: The research document *proposes*; it does not *decide*.

p.a-self-ratifying-study-skips-the-review: A study that quietly rewrites the roadmap inside itself has skipped the review where a human weighs the proposal against everything else competing for the same effort.

p.LAW-FOUR-KEEP-THE-TWO-ACTS-SEPARATE: Keep the two acts separate: the study argues, the owner decides ([`from-research-to-roadmap.md`](from-research-to-roadmap.md)).

p.LAW-FIVE-THE-DOCUMENT-CLOSES-WITH-THE-RE: The document closes with **every source URL, its access date, and the subject's version at capture** — the exact list needed to refresh the study later.

p.the-study-has-a-shelf-life: Because the subject keeps shipping, the study has a shelf life; the re-fetch list is what lets a future session *update* the study instead of starting over.

p.record-enough-that-the-refresh-is-mechan: Record enough that the refresh is mechanical:

item.REFETCH-WHAT-VERSION-THIS-CAPTURE-REFLEC: and what version number this capture reflects.

p.not-every-glance-warrants-a-full-study: Not every glance at a competitor warrants a full study. Write one when:

tr.td: Why it warrants the full genre

td.ROW-TRIGGER-BEFORE-BUILDING-IN-AN-OCCUPI: Before building in a space others occupy

td.fact: Cheaper to learn their dead ends than to re-walk them
An emotional reaction needs a structured study to become a decision

td.ROW-TRIGGER-A-RECURRING-WHY-NOT-QUESTION: "Why don't we just do what X does?" recurs

td.fact: A recurring question deserves a durable, citable answer, not a repeated verbal one

p.a-one-off-lookup-does-not-warrant-a-stud: For a one-off factual lookup — "does X support Windows?" — a study is overkill; answer it and move on.

p.THE-GENRE-IS-FOR-A-SYSTEM-WORTH-UNDERSTA: The genre is for a *system* worth understanding whole, whose shape will inform decisions more than once.

item.NOT-A-DECISION: **Not a decision.** It proposes deltas; ratification is downstream.

item.NOT-A-RANT: **Not a rant.** Competitive frustration is the trigger; the document is the disciplined product, two-way and quoted.

item.NOT-A-LIVE-DASHBOARD: **Not a live dashboard.** It is a dated snapshot with a refresh procedure — a baseline, not a feed. When it ages, refresh it via the re-fetch list; keep the old capture as historical record.

item.NOT-A-LINK-FARM: **Not a link farm.** Links rot; the quotes are the evidence.

re-derive.title: Re-derive for your project

p.re-derive-lead: Do not copy this protocol's framing verbatim — copy the *task*, and let the agent produce the study your project actually needs:

re-derive.fence: Read this flow's documents (your project installed them — typically `vibedeps/flow-comparative-research/<version>/spec/flows/comparative-research/`, check `vibe.lock`) in full, then run one study: 1. Name the external system to study and why now (building nearby / they shipped something / a recurring "why not do what X does"). 2. Fetch its primary sources — docs, pitch, changelog — and record each URL with today's date and the subject's current version. 3. Quote the subject verbatim in fenced blocks before any judgement; never critique a paraphrase. 4. Write BOTH gap directions: where we trail, where we lead, each argued with equal weight and concrete evidence. 5. Turn the actionable trailing gaps into numbered deltas, each with a priority and a target home in our spec tree. Ratify none. 6. Close with the re-fetch list. Show me the draft; apply nothing.

item.SUM-A-SELF-CONTAINED-EVERGREEN-STUDY: A comparative research document is a self-contained, evergreen study of one external system, written to outlast its own sources.

item.SUM-WHY-THE-GENRE-EXISTS: It exists because unexamined competitors cost roadmap mistakes and examined ones yield deltas — and the study must survive link rot.

item.SUM-THE-FIVE-LAWS: Five laws: self-containedness (dated verbatim quotes), quote-first then critique, two-way gaps (trail *and* lead), deltas-not-decrees (numbered, prioritized, homed, unratified), and the re-fetch list.

item.SUM-WHEN-TO-WRITE-ONE: Write one before building in an occupied space, when a competitor alarms, or when "why not do what X does" keeps recurring.

item.SUM-THE-STUDY-PROPOSES-THE-OWNER-DECIDES: The study proposes; the owner decides. See [`from-research-to-roadmap.md`](from-research-to-roadmap.md).
